name: Tambour embroidery
summary: A fast chain stitch made with a fine hook on cloth that is stretched tight in a frame; later the same hook sews beads on silk.
how: Stretch the cloth tight in a round frame.
Pull a loop of thread up through the cloth with the hook, and chain the loops along the pattern.
Thread beads on the yarn first, and chain them into the cloth to make a beaded surface.

origin.note: Tambour work from India and China reaches European workrooms in the 18th century, and it grows fast on muslin.

adoptions.via: Dressmakers sew white tambour borders on muslin gowns and shawls.
Paris embroidery houses use the hook to sew glass beads on chiffon for the dress of the 1920s.
